I'm identifying the two colored pieces - an L-shape of 4 cells and a T-shape of 5 cells, totaling 9 cells - then examining the grey shapes on the grid to find matching regions, starting with a 2x3 block that doesn't fit and checking another candidate area.

The third grey shape, a 9-cell region, actually decomposes exactly into the two pieces when I try placing the L-shape at the top and check if the remainder matches the T-shape's stem-and-row pattern - it does. I then rule out the other candidate regions since they don't match either piece's cell count or shape correctly.

I'm identifying the piece shapes - an 5-cell P-pentomino and a 3-cell diagonal king-linked piece, totaling 8 cells - then mapping out the grey shapes' cell coordinates on the grid.

Checking shape1 (7 cells) and shape2 (9 cells), neither fits the 8-cell total, so I rule them out. Shape3 has 8 cells, so I test whether it decomposes into piece A plus the diagonal triomino - placing piece A at the origin covers most of it, and the leftover cells form the exact antidiagonal shape matching the other piece, confirming shape3 as the match.

I'm sketching out three demos with similar structure, using an L-tromino plus a single cell to form tetromino assemblies, and checking whether grey shapes like an S-tetromino would match against them.

For a second demo I'm considering two dominoes without rotation allowed, realizing this constraint makes forming a square tricky since I'd need matching orientations, so I'll simplify by using two identical vertical dominoes instead.

I'll move forward with three demos and verify the outputs work as intended.
